evidence: config.py:175 — `('gemini', 'google_genai')` still maps bare gemini ids to the `google_genai` provider
tests/unit/test_provider_qualifier.py:283 — `assert _resolve_target('gemini-2.5-pro', None) == 'google_genai:gemini-2.5-pro'` confirms this composed string is still produced live
src/rebar/llm/runner.py:358-359 — for a REAL model `ran_model = resolved` (e.g. `google_genai:gemini-2.5-pro`)

src/rebar/llm/runner.py:596 — `provider=infer_provider(ran_model)` now returns None because `google_genai` ∉ KNOWN_PROVIDER_NAMES and the `_PROVIDER_PREFIXES` scan misses a string beginning `google_genai:`
src/rebar/llm/config.py:203 — the comment only justifies excluding `google_genai` as a QUALIFIER but does not account for it being a live inference OUTPUT that gets re-read by infer_provider
src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py:425 — `provider_id=row.get('provider') or None` forwards the now-missing provider into `genai_prices.calc_price`, losing the pricing disambiguation hint

ABSENCE: the diff documents only the `test:`/FunctionModel provider-omission (test_usage_log.py, test_usage_log_failed_calls.py); no test or note covers the `google_genai:`/gemini row losing its provider field
advisory.finding: Producer/consumer drift: dropping `google_genai` from `KNOWN_PROVIDER_NAMES` changes `infer_provider('google_genai:gemini-2.5-pro')` from `'google_genai'` to `None`, so the usage log silently omits the `provider` field for real gemini/google_genai runs (not just the acknowledged `test:` FunctionModel double), and passes `provider_id=None` into pricing.
scenarios: An operator runs a workflow step configured for a bare `gemini-2.5-pro` model: the usage-log rows for that run no longer carry `provider`, and pricing is computed without the provider hint.
advisory.suggested_fix: Either keep the qualifier's meaning stable for `google_genai` in `infer_provider` (e.g. have infer_provider recognize composed prefixes it emitted), or make `_resolve_target`/`_pai_model` emit the pydantic-ai canonical prefix (`google-gla`) that IS in KNOWN_PROVIDER_NAMES, so the composed target round-trips through split_provider_qualifier.

src/rebar/llm/config.py:434-438 — `model_provider` is an operator-facing OPTIONAL config field ('Set it explicitly for ambiguous names'), so a previously-valid `model_provider = 'google_genai'` in a user's config now raises

advisory.finding: Narrowed accepted input: `_resolve_target` now raises `LLMConfigError` for any explicitly-configured provider name outside `KNOWN_PROVIDER_NAMES`, where previously any identifier-shaped provider (e.g. `google_genai`, or any custom/local provider name matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*$`) was accepted and composed. Existing configs naming a provider not in the 24-name set are now rejected.
scenarios: An operator whose pyproject sets `model_provider = 'google_genai'` (or any provider name accepted by the old shape test but absent from the 24-name set) now gets a hard LLMConfigError at config resolution where it previously composed a target string.
